header: What a bakery with three branches actually took last year
subheader: From 212 shops that let us use their anonymised figures.
bodytext:
The median shop in the sample took € 41,200 a month across three counters. The spread underneath that number is the interesting part: the best quarter took more than twice what the worst quarter did, in towns of the same size, with the same opening hours.

Where the difference sits

Almost none of it is in bread. Bread volumes vary by about a tenth across the whole sample, which is roughly what the local population explains. The difference is in what is sold beside the bread between half past six and nine in the morning: coffee, one filled roll, something for later.
